assessment: The candidate handled the offer details accurately (automatic 20%, no code, exact 72-hour ET window, all exclusions, no invented compensation) and improved accountability meaningfully across revisions, explicitly owning the checkout update without future-uptime guarantees. Trust and tone are more contested: the initial draft asserted an unsupported absence of a security incident, conflated 'pending charge' with authorization, and later wording ('we will work with you individually to get it sorted') implies refunds despite unconfirmed charges. The lack of a single consolidated final post was a consistent weakness across judges.
judge_agreement: Judges broadly agreed on offer accuracy and that revisions improved ownership and tone. Disagreement centered on the speculative security claim (Anthropic counted it as a rule error; others a flag or a corrected misstep) and on whether to score the final revision standalone (deepseek, penalizing omissions) versus the full conversation. Trust and tone showed the widest spread (5-9), driven by differing weights on the initial security assurance and refund-implying language.
